questions.q: Why does Cascade's Account object need six Record Types instead of one?
options: Salesforce requires at least six Record Types on every object
A restaurant's Account looks meaningfully different from a hospital system's -- different fields and page layouts make sense for each customer segment
Record Types are required before any custom field can be created
Six Record Types is the maximum Salesforce allows, so Cascade used all of them
questions.explain: The lesson explains Record Types exist because different kinds of Cascade customers -- restaurants, hotels, hospitals, schools, caterers, and dealers -- need different picklist values and page layouts, not a one-size-fits-all Account.

questions.q: What is the functional difference between Record Type and the Business Segment custom field on Account?
options: They are identical and one is redundant
Record Type controls page layout and picklist values; Business Segment is a plain field used for simple reporting and filtering
Business Segment controls page layout; Record Type is used only for reporting
Record Type only applies to Contacts, not Accounts
questions.explain: The lesson states Record Type controls which page layout and picklist values a user sees, while Business Segment is a plain field you can report and filter on without worrying about Record Type IDs -- exactly how Chapter 4's reports use it.

questions.q: Which Contact field does a Chapter 3 validation rule reference, and what does it flag?
options: Preferred_Contact_Method__c -- flags how a rep should reach out
Contact_Role__c -- flags the person's job title only
Decision_Maker__c -- flags whether this Contact can approve a purchase
Business_Segment__c -- flags which Account segment a Contact belongs to
questions.explain: The lesson states Decision_Maker__c is a checkbox flagging whether a Contact can approve a purchase, and notes it's used later by the Opportunity-stage validation rule in Chapter 3.

questions.q: What are the four steps to creating a custom field, as described in this lesson?
options: Write Apex, deploy via change set, run tests, activate
Create a Flow, add a decision element, add an action, activate
Open Object Manager and pick the object; go to Fields & Relationships and click New; set type/label/picklist values; set field-level security
Create a report, add a filter, save, and share
questions.explain: The lesson lists these exact four steps for creating any custom field declaratively: Object Manager, Fields & Relationships > New, set the type and values, then set field-level security per profile.

questions.q: Per this lesson's field-level security guidance, which profiles get Edit access on the new Account and Contact fields, and which get Read Only?
options: Sales Rep and Sales Manager get Edit; Service and Customer Success profiles get Read Only
Only System Administrator gets any access at all
Service and Customer Success get Edit; Sales profiles get Read Only
All profiles get Edit access equally
questions.explain: The lesson specifies Sales Rep and Sales Manager get Edit access since this is sales-owned data, while Service and Customer Success profiles get Read Only.
